fatal_errors: The proposed La(Fe,Si)13 material is unrelated to the target Mn0.6Ni1−xSi0.62Fe0.4CoxGe0.38 high-entropy alloys.
The intervention does not reconstruct the systematic Co-for-Ni substitution from x = 0.40 to 0.55.

The predicted improvement with Co substitution contradicts the target result: increasing Co progressively reduced the peak magnetic entropy change and ultimately suppressed the giant first-order magnetocaloric effect at x = 0.55.
The cited evidence concerns equiatomic FeCoNiTi preparation and characterization, not La(Fe,Si)13 or the target Mn-Ni-Fe-Co-Si-Ge system, so it provides no support for the hypothesis.
explanation: The response is generically relevant to magnetocaloric compositional tuning, and its proposed measurements could test its own La(Fe,Si)13 hypothesis. However, it fails to identify the target alloy family, substitution series, processing conditions, phase transition sequence, baseline, and quantitative outcomes. Its mechanism only overlaps at the broad level of substitution changing exchange interactions and transition temperature. Most importantly, it predicts enhanced entropy change from Mn/Co modification, whereas the target study found that increasing Co-for-Ni substitution lowered transition temperatures and peak −ΔSM, with x = 0.55 changing to a weak second-order response. The sole citation is scientifically disconnected from both the proposed and target materials.
